correctness.rationale: For every nonempty block \(B\), the recent theorem gives \(U(B)=2^{|B|-1}(A_B+2)\) with \(A_B=\sum_{i\in B}(d_i-2)\), and the singleton case is the known exact rank \(d_i\). Direct expansion gives \(U(I)U(J)-U(I\cup J)=2^{|I|+|J|-2}A_IA_J\) for disjoint nonempty blocks. Since every \(d_i\ge3\), both \(A_I\) and \(A_J\) are positive. Iterating the strictly improving two-block merge proves the arbitrary-partition inequality. No finite experiment is used for the universal step.

value.rationale: The source presents a constructive many-factor decomposition, while a natural competing strategy is to decompose smaller blocks and tensor the resulting decompositions. The exact positive merge gap proves that the new construction has genuine many-factor efficiency at every split, and that no recursive blockwise use of the same bound can match the direct certified length. This is a structural statement about how the new bound composes, not a parameter renaming or a numerical spot check.
